tools.description: Run a parameter search on the remote backtest daemon (--backtest-addr) from a profile TOML with a [paramscan] table (each key overrides strategy.params.<key> across a value grid; the legacy [paramscan] spelling still loads), its [strategy] file naming a strategy file the daemon holds (an inline `script` is refused). DEFAULT is the exhaustive grid; `optimizer` selects a smarter search (euler = successive halving, tpe = Bayesian, genetic) and each method takes its own knob — a knob under a method that does not own it is REFUSED by name, never discarded. Returns the server-ranked search, one row per grid point, best first: each row's overrides, its report (every metric-catalog number, keyed by metric id: sharpe, total_return, max_drawdown, n_trades, profit_factor, ...), error and score, the rows paged in for you; no trades and no curves, which stay in the run the daemon saved (saved_run; point N is that run's report.json rows[N-1]). A top-level `strategy_failures` (every point's together) means the strategy failed during the search: say so first, the ranking is not trustworthy. An older daemon answers the whole ParamscanReport (each row's whole TradingResults) instead. Cancellable: notifications/cancelled drops the response and closes the daemon connection, and the daemon stops evaluating grid points once it sees the connection gone. With background: true it answers a run_id at once and runs on: run_status reads it, cancel_run stops it.

tools.description: Run an out-of-sample walk-forward on the remote backtest daemon (--backtest-addr) from a profile TOML with a [walkforward] table, its [strategy] file naming a strategy file the daemon holds (an inline `script` is refused). DEFAULT (n_splits alone) is the FIXED-parameter stability walk: every window trades the profile's own [strategy.params] and chooses nothing — do NOT report such a run as an optimization. search = "paramscan" in [walkforward] runs the other protocol: each window re-scores the [paramscan] grid on its OWN training half and trades only that window's winner (mode = anchored|rolling, rank_by = sharpe|return|max_dd|equity); it needs a [paramscan] table and is refused without one. Returns the stitched walk-forward results JSON (steps, each with its own out-of-sample results, + the overall results of the stitched curve + profitable_step_share; the curve itself, `equity_curve`, only with include_curve: true) — only a step that searched carries chosen_params, which is how you tell the two runs apart. A `strategy_failures` key in overall (or a step's results) means the strategy failed there: say so first, those numbers are not trustworthy. Run both on one profile: the no-search control is the only evidence that searching bought anything. Cancellable: notifications/cancelled drops the response and closes the daemon connection, and the daemon stops starting windows (and, under search = "paramscan", training-half grid points) once it sees the connection gone. With background: true it answers a run_id at once and runs on: run_status reads it, cancel_run stops it.

include_curve.description: also answer the stitched out-of-sample `equity_curve`, one point a bar: most of the answer (hundreds of KB for a year of 30-minute bars). Default false: the curve is left out

tools.description: Read the running vike-tradehub's live state (orders, positions, per-venue equity, recent events). An order the node HOLDS until a moment (submit_order's release_at) is not in `orders` yet: it is in `held_exits` with its `release`, and cancel_order cancels it by its order_client_id. The frame's `bars` are left out, so the answer stays small enough for a client to show. ⚠ Top-level `positions`, `balance` and `trading_state` are the PRIMARY engine's alone and `equity_total` covers only its currency group, so on a node with several accounts read `venues[].positions` before calling anything flat. Requires --node and this box's device key on the node's access list (role observe or higher). If the result carries `pre_fold: true`, the frame holds nothing built: with `identity` present it is the placeholder the node publishes before its first fold; with `identity: null` it is this client's own placeholder, because no node frame arrived in time. Either way venues, balance, equity_total and accounts_epoch are placeholders, `venues: []` does NOT mean nothing is mounted, and `pre_fold_note` says which — call it again. If the node connection has dropped, this returns an ERROR naming it DOWN and the last frame STALE, never that frame as if live, and reconnects on the next call, so call it again rather than restarting anything. ⚠ A link that dies SILENTLY (a sleeping laptop, an ssh tunnel without ServerAliveInterval) is noticed only once the node's heartbeat has been missing for about 45 s, and never on a node too old to send one: until then the last frame is answered as live, and the frame carries no timestamp to age it by. If the picture never changes while the node should be trading, have the operator check the tunnel before trusting it.

tools.description: Ask the running vike-tradehub WHAT IT IS RUNNING: which daemon answered (name, live/paper, build), the daemon's resolved effective-params line, and one row per strategy the node runs NOW, a mount added while it runs included and an unmounted one gone. A row carries the strategy name, that mount's params, its `mount_id` (the id unmount_strategy takes), `venue`/`symbol`/`interval`, `typed_params`, `route_key` (the account it trades), `tier` (the tier that account runs at now: paper, demo or live), `not_running` (present when the node does not run that account, so its orders are refused) and `live` (its orders reach a venue, so a demo account reads true: read `tier`; it may disagree with the daemon's own live flag). A field a node predates is absent from its rows. Read-only, over the OBSERVE scope: it can neither place nor change anything. Requires --node and this box's device key on the node's access list (role observe or higher) and a node that advertises the strategy verbs; an older node is refused CLIENT-SIDE with nothing sent.

tools.description: Read the running vike-tradehub's EFFECTIVE settings: `settings_dir`, the settings directory it resolved at boot (null = compiled-in defaults), then `rows`, one per typed key: its `section` (the key's first segment), its full dotted `key`, the effective `value` (empty = unset), its `origin`, the layer that set it (`default` or `db`), and `read_by`, what actually READS it. ⚠ A `refusal` beside them means the node could not read its settings database or does not trust it: every row may then be a compiled-in default reading `origin: default`, a ceiling as absent, so report the refusal and none of the rows. Sensitive-looking values arrive already redacted by the node. Read-only, over the OBSERVE scope. Requires --node and this box's device key on the node's access list (role observe or higher) and a node that advertises the settings-show capability; an older node is refused CLIENT-SIDE with nothing sent. `rows[].key` is the exact spelling set_setting takes.

tools.description: Judge the running vike-tradehub in one call: the `vike-cli trade health --json` document. `verdict` (OK | WARN | FAIL), the `warn`, `fail` and `unknown` counts, and `checks[]`, one row per finding as {status, check, account, detail, items}: is its door ready, which accounts run and at which tier or are NOT RUNNING and why, halted or reducing venues, held reconcile rows, resting orders, positions with no price, the HALT sentinel. An UNKNOWN row is a fact the wire does not carry and names the command that answers it; it does not move the verdict. Plus `gatewayhub`, that daemon as the datahub (--addr) sees it: {via, reached, error, uptime_ms, epoch, connections, stream_sessions, fetches_running, market_data_venues, credentialed_data_venues}; it says nothing of any venue. ⚠ A dead tradehub is a RESULT here, not an error: `verdict: FAIL` and a row saying it does not answer, so read `verdict`. Read-only, over the OBSERVE scope: no command, no event. Requires --node and this box's device key on the node's access list (role observe or higher).

tools.title: Check node health

tools.description: Read ONE live account's trading results: its own fills out of the datahub (--addr) over the window, its tier and its ledgers from the vike-tradehub's snapshot, folded into the realized round-trips and their metrics, the same document `vike-cli report account:<venue>/<LABEL> --json` prints. `name` heads it with the account, its tier and its period, then says what was counted or left out, one sentence each: the starting capital and where it came from, FOREIGN fills (placed outside this install, on the account all the same, so they count), fills recorded before the execution stream (they name no account, so they are left out). The curve is the REALIZED one, from `cash`; `cash` and `periods_per_year` rescale the ratios. A refusal is an ERROR here, never an empty report: an account the node names nowhere or does not run (its ledger and contracts are then unknown), a symbol its kept row or its name quotes off the dollar or in no known currency, a datahub that records no live executions, an opening position nothing can read. It reads no finished backtest: that report is what run_backtest returned. Read-only. Requires --node and this box's device key on the node's access list (role observe or higher), and a datahub that records live executions.

tools.description: Set the trading state / kill switch of every account on the node — active | reducing | halted. WITHOUT confirm:true this only PREVIEWS. ⚠ It is NOT a venue arming control and cannot start or stop an account or change its tier: what an account runs at is its ACCOUNT ROW in the settings database's account table — its tier (paper | demo | live) and whether it is active. With no row, an inactive row, missing keys or two active tiers that account is NOT RUNNING and its orders are refused; nothing trades on paper in its place. A human changes the row on the box with the vike-cli `account set-tier` / `account activate` / `account deactivate` verbs, the running node follows it within about a second with no restart, and nothing on this server can change it.

tools.description: Add ONE strategy mount to the running vike-tradehub's core, LIVE and without a restart. WITHOUT confirm:true this only PREVIEWS (executes nothing). The source is the `strategy` file: its path under the NODE's strategies/ folder (a .rs or .rhai file) — not script source, and not a path on this machine; this server cannot put a file on that box. `venue` must name an engine the node already runs — read it from node_snapshot's venues[].venue. The node validates at its edge with the same refusals a profile load applies; a refusal the core itself raises later (a duplicate mount id, an unknown venue) surfaces in the node's recent events rather than here. Requires a node that advertises the mount verbs; an older one is refused CLIENT-SIDE with nothing sent.

OMIT it only where the node has ONE account of that venue, running or not: where it has two or more, an account-less mount is REFUSED rather than sent to the default one, because the default account's route key IS the bare venue and the silent answer would look correct. Pass "DEFAULT" to name the venue's unlabelled account deliberately — that is a DIFFERENT thing from omitting the field, and it is accepted at any account count

tools.description: Write ONE setting on the running node: one row of its settings database, named by its full dotted `key` (policy.* | config.* | preferences.* | flags.*) and validated by the NODE's own loader before it commits — so a write can never leave a store the next boot refuses. WITHOUT confirm:true AND this call's preview_token it only PREVIEWS, and the preview's `change` shows the key's current value on the node beside the new one (old → new). ⚠ This changes a LIVE setting on the node, and a policy.* key is a risk ceiling or an arming switch: confirm one only after the owner said yes in chat. A session started with --unattended refuses every key; settings are then changed by the operator, with `vike-cli config set` or the GUI. The answer's `restart_required` says which happened: false = the node applied the value LIVE, true = it applies at the next restart (every policy.* key — policy is never hot). Read settings_show first: `rows[].key` is the exact spelling this takes. Requires a node that advertises the settings-write capability; an older one is refused CLIENT-SIDE with nothing sent.

tools.description: DELETE stored data series from the datahub's history store, IRREVERSIBLY. Selects on the four series dimensions: `kind` and `venue` are required, and an OMITTED `symbol`/`group`/`interval` is a wildcard over that dimension (there are no globs — omission is the only wildcard). ⚠ `produced_by` is REQUIRED on EVERY call here, unlike the `vike-cli data history rm` command, where it is optional for a fully-named series: every commit key of every matched series must carry that prefix, and ONE foreign key refuses the whole run and deletes nothing. That is deliberate — you compose an identity from context that may be stale, and a provenance assertion is the one check that fails on a plausible-but-wrong one. WITHOUT confirm:true AND a matching preview_token this only PLANS: it returns which series matched, what each holds, and the commit keys that wrote them, with `matched`/`rows`/`bytes` as numbers to compare against what you expected. Read `list_series` first if you are unsure what the store holds. Deletion cannot be undone, and a window a venue no longer serves cannot be re-fetched at all. Requires this box's device key on the datahub's access list (role control or higher) — a key-less datahub serves no delete verb.

confirm.description: must be true AND accompanied by a valid `preview_token` to execute; either one missing returns a preview instead

group.description: the EXACT group of a GROUPED series (which holds many symbols in one part and has NO symbol of its own). Alternative to `symbol`

interval.description: the EXACT bar interval (`1h`). Omit to wildcard; refused together with `group`, whose leaf has no interval segment

kind.description: the EXACT stored kind (bar | quote | trade | book | depth | properties | …), never a substring

preview_token.description: the `preview_token` returned by this tool's preview call. Fires ONCE, expires after 60s, and is BOUND to the exact command it previewed — confirming a different command with it is refused.

produced_by.description: REQUIRED. The commit-key PREFIX every key of every matched series must carry (`panel_bars:`, `pmxt:quote:`). ⚠ A LITERAL prefix, never a producer PATH: this tool deletes through a datahub, and a path is refused here before anything is dialled. `vike-cli data history rm --dry-run` reports each series' keys, or ask the operator — that is evidence from the store, where a path is a guess about a source tree you cannot see; and a datahub that has not been redeployed since 2026-09-11 resolves no path at all, so one sent there would be asserted literally, match no key, and report the store as foreign when in fact the argument was never resolved. One key that does not carry it refuses the whole run. There is no override and no --force.

reason.description: optional rationale — WHY this command is being issued. Recorded in the node's audit trail (control characters stripped, capped at 512 chars); never reaches the order, the core, or the venue.

symbol.description: the EXACT symbol of a PER-SYMBOL series. Omit to wildcard the dimension. Alternative to `group`, never a pair

venue.description: the EXACT venue slug, never a substring. ⚠ It names an EXCHANGE, never a data SOURCE — rows fetched from a metrics vendor land under the exchange they describe, which is why `produced_by` is the only thing that tells two producers of one series apart
